To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aggressive pulmonary hygiene care and the addition of tigecyclin to colistin are beneficial in improving the clinical outcome of patients with nonbacteremic pneumonia caused XDR-Acb.
the addition of TIGECYLIN to aerosolized COLISTIMETHATE SODIUM therapy improved the 14-day outcome of patients with XDR-ACINETOBACTER CALCOACETICUS-ACINETOBACTER BAUMANNII COMPLEX pneumonia.
the addition of standard-dose TGC to AS-CMS treatment did not improve the 30-day mortality in patients with nonbacteremic XDR- Acb pneumonia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical efficacy of AS-CMS monotherapy or in combination with TGC in patients with non- bacteremic pneumonia due to Acb complex isolates.
the treatment of patients with XDR-Acb non-bacteremic pneumonic infections.
the treatment outcomes of patients with XDR-Acb non-bacteremic community-acquired pneumonia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AS-CMS plus TGC was not superior to AS-CMS alone in curing XDR-Acb non-bacteremic patients’ pneumonia.
the combination of AS-CMS with TGC was not beneficial for the treatment of patients with XDR-Acb non-bacteremic community-acquired pneumonia.
the combination therapy with TGC plus AS-Colistin was not associated with a better 30-day outcome than AS-Colistin therapy alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 14-day outcome of XDR-Acb non-bacteremic pneumonic patients was not improved by adding TGC to the AS-CMS therapy.
the 30-day survival rate was not significantly different between the 2 treatment groups.

the combination of TGC and AS-CMS therapy was associated with a higher 30-day case-fatal rate, and this might be due to the emergence of colisitin-resistant Acb isolators in the airway specimens of patients with nonbacteremic XDR Acb pneumonia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
XDR-Acb infection is a serious threat to the patients with pneumonia.
the 14-day mortality rate was the best predictor of the 30-day outcome in patients with nonbacteremic XDR- Acb pneumonia.
the combination of AS-CMS with TGC is not superior to AS-CMS therapy alone for treating non-bacteremic, XDR-Acb-complex pneumonia.
